title: Consequences: sonship; Spirit of adoption; Cap.20 next
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY follows, On Christian warfare and ye cross. — XI–XII. Ye right belonging toward sons stands as that they stand as heirs belonging toward God and co-heirs with Christ, including ye body's liberation from vanity; ye Spirit belonging toward adoption assures us belonging toward coming glory. — X. A consequence belonging toward liberty from sin and law—to which peace belonging toward conscience stands as annexed—is both ye right belonging toward God's children and ye sending belonging toward ye Spirit belonging toward adoption into believers' hearts.
pass_b_english: X. A consequence of liberty from sin and law—to which peace of conscience is annexed—is both the right of God's children and the sending of the Spirit of adoption into believers' hearts.
XI–XII. The right of sons is that they are heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, including the body's liberation from vanity; the Spirit of adoption assures us of coming glory.
CHAPTER TWENTY follows, On Christian warfare and the cross.
source_text: X. Consequens libertatis e servitute peccati et legis, cui pax conscientiae annectitur, est tum ius filiorum Dei, tum missio Spiritus adoptionis in corda fidelium. XI. Ius filiorum Dei est quod constituti sunt heredes Dei et cohaeredes Christi—etiam liberatio corporum a vanitate (Rom. 8:15-23). XII. Missio Spiritus adoptionis nos certos reddit gloriae futurae. CAPUT VIGESIMUM sequitur, De militia et cruce Christiana.
